subsystems.name: Mobile robot platform
subsystems.role: carries goods across the warehouse floor; fleets are built from many identical units rather than a few big machines.

subsystems.name: Onboard perception and localisation
subsystems.role: lets each robot know where it is and what is in front of it, indoors where GPS does not work.

subsystems.name: Task allocation layer
subsystems.role: decides which robot takes which job.

subsystems.name: Traffic and deadlock layer
subsystems.role: keeps hundreds of robots from blocking each other in narrow aisles.
parts: reservation of map cells with expiry times

subsystems.name: Stigmergic environment layer
subsystems.role: robots coordinate indirectly by leaving traces in a shared world model rather than talking to each other.
parts: virtual pheromone fields that grow with congestion and decay over time

subsystems.name: Communication and edge compute
subsystems.role: links robots, charging bays and the warehouse software.
parts: dense indoor Wi-Fi or private cellular

subsystems.name: Warehouse interface
subsystems.role: connects the swarm to shelves, conveyors and human pickers.

buildSteps.title: Map the building as a traffic grammar
buildSteps.detail: The floor is divided into a grid of cells with one-way lanes, passing places, charging bays and no-go zones for people.

buildSteps.title: Instrument the environment
buildSteps.detail: Floor markers or ceiling tags are fitted, radio coverage is surveyed, and a site map is calibrated so every robot shares one coordinate frame.

buildSteps.title: Build the robot
buildSteps.detail: A simple chassis with drive motors, a lift or conveyor deck, a battery and a rugged onboard computer is assembled and tested.

buildSteps.title: Write local navigation
buildSteps.detail: Each robot runs localisation, obstacle avoidance and a safety-rated emergency stop entirely on board, so it can still behave safely if the network drops.

buildSteps.title: Design the coordination protocol
buildSteps.detail: Jobs are offered to nearby robots through a bidding rule; a winner reserves the cells along its route for a set time, and stale reservations expire automatically.

buildSteps.title: Add the stigmergic layer
buildSteps.detail: Software pheromones are deposited on congested cells and decay each second, so the colony of robots drifts away from jams without any central controller issuing each move.

buildSteps.title: Simulate at scale
buildSteps.detail: Thousands of virtual robots run against the real map and order stream to find deadlocks and throughput limits before any hardware moves.

buildSteps.title: Integrate and commission
buildSteps.detail: A handful of robots is run alongside human pickers, then the fleet is ramped up while throughput, collisions and charging behaviour are measured.

buildSteps.title: Tune for heterogeneous fleets
buildSteps.detail: Robots with different sizes, speeds and payloads are given weights in the same reservation system so they can share aisles.

prerequisites.why: each robot needs centimetre-to-decimetre accuracy using lidar, cameras or fiducials.
hundreds of robots exchanging state need reliable coverage without dead spots.

prerequisites.tech: Multi-agent task allocation and deadlock-free routing
prerequisites.why: provably collision-free, deadlock-free planning is solved in research settings but harder on a messy real floor.
robots sharing space with pickers must detect people and stop reliably, which is regulated engineering, not just software.

prerequisites.tech: Cheap high-cycle batteries and opportunity charging
prerequisites.why: swarms only pay off if robots charge in short bursts instead of being swapped out by hand.
coordination only makes economic sense when each unit is inexpensive enough to field in hundreds.

pathway.milestone: centrally managed fleets of hundreds of mobile robots moving shelves and totes, common in large e-commerce warehouses
pathway.unlocks: high-throughput goods-to-person picking with far less walking.

pathway.milestone: decentralised task auctions and stigmergic congestion signalling running in pilots alongside central control
pathway.unlocks: simpler scaling to larger fleets and no single point of failure.

pathway.milestone: mixed fleets of robots, automated forklifts and manipulators sharing one reservation layer
pathway.unlocks: one coordination system across a whole site instead of separate islands per vendor.

pathway.milestone: open, verifiable swarm protocols across sites and outdoor yards
pathway.unlocks: robots that can hand off loads between buildings, yards and delivery vehicles without a central dispatcher.
